rows.text: The Ops Engineer shall open a triage channel within 5 minutes of page acknowledgement.
The Operations Engineer must capture the initial alert payload and paste it into the channel.
The engineer shall page the on-call Platform Lead if the incident is not acknowledged within 10 minutes.
The Platform Lead must join the triage channel and assume incident command.
The Platform-Lead shall designate a scribe and a communicator within the first 15 minutes of the incident.
At 02:00 local, the system shall begin a full snapshot of the primary data volume.
The system must verify snapshot integrity before promoting the image to the off-site store.
A summary report shall be emailed to the on-call distribution list once the run completes.
If verification fails, the system must retain the primary volume in read-write mode and page the on-call engineer.
Retention policy shall prune snapshots older than 30 days.

rows.text: The Account Manager shall validate the customer identification before creating any account.
The Compliance Officer must review the validation result within two business days.
The Account Manager shall notify the customer of the approval decision via the registered email address.
The QA Lead shall begin the smoke-test suite against the release candidate build.
The Release Manager must stage the deployment package in the canary environment.
The QA Lead shall record smoke-test results in the release tracker within 30 minutes.
The Release Manager must confirm canary health telemetry for at least 10 minutes before promotion.
The QA Lead shall sign off on the release once all smoke tests pass.
The Release Manager must promote the canary to production only after QA sign-off.
If any smoke test fails, the QA Lead shall halt the release and notify the Release Manager.
On halt, the Release Manager must roll back the canary and capture diagnostic logs for the post-mortem.
Each change request shall be reviewed by the Change Board before any production deployment.
Approval must be granted by the Security Officer when the change touches authentication flows.
A rollback plan shall be signed off by the Release Manager prior to the change window.
Post-change validation must be completed by the Duty Engineer within 30 minutes of deployment.
The Operator shall log in to the control console and confirm the previous shift's handover notes.
Verify that all subsystem status indicators read nominal and acknowledge any outstanding alarms.
The Supervisor must review the overnight alarm log before releasing the Operator to normal duties.
Countersign the handover log once the checks are complete.
The Operator shall acknowledge receipt of the countersigned log and begin normal shift duties.
The Release Manager shall confirm that the build ID in the tracker matches the artifact SHA-256 in the pipeline.
The QA Lead shall execute the following smoke checks:
Run the authentication smoke-test suite and record pass/fail per case.
Exercise the canary endpoint with a synthetic payload under nominal load.
Confirm that the error budget dashboard is still green before clearing the gate.
If any smoke check fails, halt the release and notify the on-call Release Manager immediately.
Before granting the final approval the Change Board must:
Review the rollback plan and confirm it executes cleanly against the staging environment.
Verify that the Security Officer has signed off when the change touches authentication flows.
Record the approval decision and the quorum in the change register before the change window opens.
The Actor column enumerates the eligible services; the Required action column's sentence subject names the one that actually carries out the step for a given row.
The Gateway shall forward the incoming authentication request to the Auth Service without modification.
The Auth Service must verify the signed token against the published public key before any session state is created.
The Logger shall emit a structured audit entry containing the request ID, the verifying service, and the outcome.
If the verification fails, the error shall be returned to the caller with HTTP status 401 and no session token.
Written in indicative voice throughout — no shall / must / should / may.
Each row is a requirement by virtue of the Required action column header, not by virtue of any modal keyword in the sentence.

The Operator reviews the previous shift's handover notes before touching any control surface.
The Supervisor validates the active alarm list and acknowledges any outstanding items.
The Supervisor records the go/no-go decision for the shift in the shift log.
The Operator acknowledges the go decision and transitions the console to normal operating mode.
